fx_note: AFI.NZ is the NZX listing (NZD-quoted) of an ASX-primary, AUD-reporting company (AFI.AX). All fundamental data (NTA, dividends, income) is AUD. current_price and all intrinsic_value/entry_price fields are reported in NZD (to match the NZX quote the user tracks) by converting the AUD-derived valuation at the live AUDNZD rate. The parallel 'aud' sub-object under each block gives the native-currency figures for direct comparison against AFI.AX.
valuation_philosophy: AFIC is a closed-end listed investment company (LIC), not an operating business - it holds a ~A$9.8bn diversified portfolio of predominantly ASX-listed blue-chip equities and passes through dividend income and capital gains to shareholders. A standard FCF DCF is inapplicable: reported 'free cash flow' is just portfolio dividend flow-through with no reinvestment/growth capex dynamic, SBC is nil, and the balance sheet is a securities portfolio rather than productive assets. Instead this model uses an NTA (net tangible assets) total-return compounding framework, standard for LIC/holdco valuation (consistent with the FIH.U and FRFHF models in this research folder): (1) project pre-tax NTA per share forward using a total-return assumption (market return net of AFIC's demonstrated benchmark underperformance and its ~0.14% MER) split between per-share NTA growth and the dividend payout; (2) apply a scenario exit premium/discount to NTA, since AFIC has persistently traded at a discount and that discount (not a P/E or EV/EBITDA multiple) is the market-clearing valuation metric for LICs; (3) headline intrinsic value = current pre-tax NTA per share x (1 + scenario fair discount) - i.e. what the market should be willing to pay for today's known NTA at a fair (rather than currently depressed) discount; (4) a separate 5-year IRR build (PV of interim dividends + PV of year-5 exit value, discounted at cost of equity) is shown as a cross-check/memo, capturing the compounding of NTA growth over the horizon rather than just today's static NTA.

inputs.dps_franking: fully franked (no benefit to NZX-domiciled holders)
inputs.sbc_note: Not applicable - AFIC is an internally-managed investment company; no stock-based compensation or dilution mechanic exists in this model.
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable - see valuation_philosophy. No FCF projection, WACC-Gordon terminal value, or SBC adjustment is used; those schema fields are replaced by the NTA-compounding equivalents below.
inputs.fx_note: Portfolio, NTA and earnings are AUD (AFIC is an ASX-listed LIC); AFI.NZ quotes NZD. Per-share values computed in AUD then converted to NZD -- see inputs.fx_rate_aud_nzd. Canonical weighted_iv is the NZD figure (weighted_iv_source=weighted_iv_nzd) so it is comparable to current_price; weighted_iv_aud is the native basis.
inputs.currency_field_note: Normalized 2026-09-01 to a bare ISO code (was 'AUD (fundamentals) / NZD (reported valuation outputs)'). The dual basis is now expressed by quote_currency + fx_note, not crammed into the code field. No valuation number changed.

historical_growth.methodology: AFIC's own preferred value driver is NTA-per-share TOTAL RETURN (NTA growth + dividends paid, since AFIC distributes nearly all income). Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs are shown for schema completeness but are NOT the growth driver used in projections - they are noisy for an LIC because reported NPAT/EPS is dominated by realised capital gains timing (large in FY2019, FY2022; small in FY2020, FY2025) rather than an operating growth trend.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nta_total_return_base_case_assumption (not a pure historical CAGR - see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue/EPS CAGRs are materially negative or muted over 3yr while NTA total return and equity CAGR are positive - this reflects realised-gains timing in reported income, not a change in underlying portfolio quality. Do not use revenue/EPS CAGR as the growth driver for this ticker.
historical_growth.notes: AFIC's own 10-year grossed-up (franking-inclusive) investment return is 10.4% p.a. vs a 9.5% grossed-up benchmark - i.e. AFIC has narrowly beaten its benchmark gross of franking over 10 years despite badly trailing it (0.9% vs 7.2%) in FY2026 alone and over 1/3/5yr periods per the Analysis JSON. This model's 6.3-6.6% computed NTA-total-return CAGR (net of franking, per-share basis) is more conservative than AFIC's own grossed-up figure and appropriate for NZX holders who cannot use franking credits. The base-case 7.5% total-return assumption sits between the trailing NTA-total-return CAGR (~6.3-6.6%) and long-run ASX equity return expectations (~9-10% grossed up), reflecting a view that AFIC's recent (FY2025/26) underperformance partly normalises but a modest structural drag versus the index persists.

base.rationale: Long-run ASX total return net of AFIC's demonstrated ~1-2pp benchmark underperformance and 0.14% MER; exit discount reverts to AFIC's long-run average (~-6%), supported by the stepped-up A$243m FY2026 buyback programme and new CEO focus on narrowing the discount.

bull.rationale: Portfolio underperformance reverses (quality names CSL/ARB/James Hardie/CAR Group recover), gold/resources underweight stops being a headwind, and aggressive buybacks plus improved market communication under new CEO Alison Gibson bring the discount to par.

bear.rationale: Underperformance persists structurally, ASX returns are muted from elevated starting valuations (management's own caution on P/E), and secular LIC demand decline versus ETFs keeps the discount at its current wide level.

five_year_irr_build_memo.description: Cross-check to the headline 'current NTA x fair discount' intrinsic value: PV of the 5-year dividend stream plus PV of the year-5 exit value (year-5 NTA x scenario exit discount), both discounted at the 8.75% cost of equity. This captures compounding of NTA growth over the horizon that the simpler current-NTA framing does not.

base.terminal_pct_of_value: n/a - not an FCF DCF; see five_year_irr_build_memo (exit value is ~81% of the 5yr-build fair value)
base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - LIC valuation uses P/NTA, not an earnings multiple

entry_price.methodology: Price today such that 5 years of projected base-case dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NTA x base-case -6% exit discount) discounted at 15% equals that price. Uses base-case cashflows only (per dcf-analyst methodology).
entry_price.memo: A 15% IRR hurdle applied to an asset whose base-case total return is only ~7.5% p.a. mechanically requires buying at a very deep discount to today's NTA (~-30% P/NTA, versus AFIC's historical range of roughly -13% to +15%) - deeper than AFIC has traded at in the observable history. This is the expected and correct output for this asset class: an ultra-low-beta, low-growth blue-chip LIC cannot organically generate a 15% forward IRR from current NTA without an implausibly large discount widening further and then reverting, so the entry price should be read as 'this is not a 15%-IRR opportunity at any normal price' rather than as an achievable near-term target. The prospective 5-year IRR from buying at today's actual price (A$6.86 / NZ$8.27) under the base case is approximately 9.7% p.a. (dividends + NTA compounding + partial discount narrowing), which is a more realistic assessment of AFIC's return prospects for a buy-and-hold holder.

sanity_check.description: For an LIC the natural sanity anchor is price/NTA, not price/earnings or EV/FCF. All scenario intrinsic values are constructed directly from the pre-tax NTA per share and are within (base, bear) or at the edge of (bull, at par) AFIC's own disclosed historical P/NTA range of roughly -13% (widest discount) to +15% (widest premium), so they pass by construction.
sanity_check.note: Current market price (-13.5% to NTA) sits at the extreme wide end of AFIC's own disclosed historical discount range, consistent with the Analysis JSON's description of a 'persistently wide (~11-13%) discount' as a live, unresolved issue. The bear case intrinsic value (-13% discount) is therefore very close to today's actual price - i.e. the market is currently pricing something close to the bear scenario already.

sensitivity.methodology: 5-year IRR-build fair value (PV of dividends + PV of exit value at year-5 NTA x row exit discount, both discounted at 8.75% cost of equity) in AUD, converted to NZD at 1.19807.
